notes.short: The old rites, a shadow; the body belongs to Christ
notes.about: The things verse 16 names, what is eaten or drunk, a feast, a New Moon or a Sabbath, are called a shadow of the things to come. A shadow has the outline of what casts it, and here “the body that casts it belongs to Christ”: what those things pictured is found in Him.

figure.name: Type
figure.words: a shadow of the things to come
figure.means: the rites of the law, outlines pointing ahead to Christ, the reality that casts the shadow

original.note: In Paul's Greek the shadow, skia, is set against the body, soma: the faint outline against the solid thing.

notes.evidence: Clarke says all these things were types, in force till the Christ they represented came. Fausset (Jamieson, Fausset and Brown) calls the ordinances the type. Barnes and Calvin say they prefigured what is in Christ; Barry (Ellicott's commentary), that the law's ritual foreshadows the substance.
notes.limit: The writers apply the shadow to the ceremonies of the law; how the verse bears on a weekly day of rest is not taken up here.

cites.quote: All these things were types, and must continue in force till the Christ, whom they represented, came ... The word σκια, shadow, is often used to express any thing imperfect or unsubstantial; while the term σωμα, body, was used in the opposite sense, and expressed any thing substantial, solid, and firm.
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: They were only a dim outline of future things, not the reality. ... Between those things themselves which are in Christ, and those which only represented or prefigured them, there is as much difference as there is between a body and a shadow; a solid substance and a mere outline.
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: the blessings of the Christian covenant, the substance of which Jewish ordinances were but the type. ... The real substance (of the blessings typified by the law) belongs to Christ
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: For the substance of those things which the ceremonies anciently prefigured is now presented before our eyes in Christ, inasmuch as he contains in himself everything that they marked out as future.

When he turns to its ritual aspect, he describes it as simply foreshadowing or typifying the substance; and therefore useful before the revelation of the substance, useless or (if trusted in) worse than useless, after it.
